records.finding: Two distinct cases demand passive channel transport down a stated gradient and an ATP-coupled pump against it. The second case changes energy availability and explicitly avoids guessing the passive ion direction. The actual image separates a passive water channel from an ATP-coupled pump; its direct-diffusion panel serves as context and is not claimed as protein-mediated ion transport.

The first case requires a controlled concentration series at fixed enzyme amount and volume, explaining rise and plateau through occupied active sites. The transfer case changes enzyme amount and rejects an unsupported fixed plateau height. The image has equal enzyme count and liquid levels, concentration on the horizontal axis, and a qualitative plateau; it is a model, not measured data.

Two separate diagram cases each provide a concrete depicted inhibitor example: one competes at the active site, and one binds at a side site with a changed active site. The profile requires binding-site and causal-effect explanations for each and does not infer medicinal efficacy. The current two-panel image depicts the same distinct mechanisms legibly.
